Physical_Process: Compaction & pore space alteration by melt/snowfall
Spatial_Uniformity: Strongly Heterogeneous (High in Palmer Land; zero on melt tongues)
Sign_Effect_on_Altimetry: Subtracted from dh/dt to isolate solid ice thinning
Critical_Vulnerabilities: Does not capture catastrophic firn collapse or ice slab formation

Physical_Process: Viscoelastic solid Earth rebound from deglaciation
Primary_Source: Regional low-viscosity models (Nield 2014, Barletta 2018) vs W12a
Spatial_Uniformity: Extremely Heterogeneous (+2 mm/yr south, +15 mm/yr north)
Sign_Effect_on_Altimetry: Subtracted from dh/dt (bedrock rises, masking true ice loss)
Critical_Vulnerabilities: Peninsula slab window causes 5x larger uplift than continental models (+/- 10 Gt/yr uncertainty)

Physical_Process: Instantaneous elastic rebound from recent ice unloading
Primary_Source: Regional elastic Green's function models constrained by GPS
Spatial_Uniformity: Concentrated near collapsed Larsen A/B outlet glaciers
Critical_Vulnerabilities: Requires knowledge of contemporary ice loss to compute correction

Physical_Process: Ku-band radar scattering horizon shifts in firn
Primary_Source: CPOM radar waveform retracking; RACMO melt detection
Spatial_Uniformity: Intense on Larsen C and Graham Land; minimal in cold Palmer Land
Typical_Magnitude_Peninsula: Apparent dh shifts of 0.5 to 4.5 m during summer melt
Sign_Effect_on_Altimetry: Falsely mimics rapid ice thickening when radar returns to surface
Critical_Vulnerabilities: Must mask out summer melt days or apply dual-frequency / SARIn retracking

Physical_Process: Laser footprint geolocation displacement on steep terrain
Primary_Source: GLAS GLA12 quality flags & REMA slope model
Spatial_Uniformity: Catastrophic in Graham Land alpine fjords; negligible on Palmer plateau
Sign_Effect_on_Altimetry: Introduces pseudo-elevation trends if repeat tracks are shifted horizontally
Critical_Vulnerabilities: Restricts ICESat-1 utility in northern Peninsula to slopes < 2 degrees
